simple.meaning: מֶכֶר (meker) is a Hebrew word meaning “merchandise ; also value.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מֶכֶר (H4377) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Numbers 20:19, with occurrences in Numbers, Nehemiah, Proverbs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מֶכֶר (H4377) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מֶכֶר (H4377) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מֶכֶר (meker) / H4377 is traced through Numbers 20:19, Nehemiah 13:16, Proverbs 31:10 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The children of Israel said to him, “We will go up by the highway; and if we drink your water, I and my livestock, then I will give its price. Only let me, without doing anything else, pass through on my feet.”
